configuration: Five-day, one-thread, binary64 run of the official 6-arc-minute Mozambique map with generated analytic daily runoff and a 10-minute multi-station tidal boundary; the final daily frame is graded.
observable: Final-cell river outflow, flood depth, flood storage, and bifurcation-channel outflow
runtime_note: under 300 s; SAB_DAYS shortens or extends the routed window
default_vs_upstream: official deck and map, shortened from 120 to 5 days and started from zero storage with generated forcing
variant: The analytic runoff rate is advanced by two binary32 ulps, from 0.0125 to 0.01250000186264515 m/day; this is the smallest perturbation retained in the netCDF forcing and calibrates numerical sensitivity without changing the routing problem.
altbuild: none: the container carries one supported gfortran build configuration, so no independent compiler or floating-point-mode floor is available

comparison.rule: For every listed physical field at every structured-grid cell, require |candidate - reference| <= 1e-3 + 1e-3 * |reference|; grid-cell position is physical, while run metadata, build timings, and storage layout are excluded.

evidence.floor_how: No altbuild is declared; numerical sensitivity is measured by nominal versus the two-ulp forcing variant on Colima arm64 and corroborated by the native TACC x86_64 run.

warrant: The human-approved 1e-3 absolute plus 1e-3 relative bound allows a 0.1% implementation-scale difference in semi-implicit local-inertial routing while rejecting a dropped bifurcation, reversed gradient, missing floodplain term, or materially wrong sea-level boundary. On Colima arm64, the two-binary32-ulp runoff perturbation used at most 0.0263 of this bound, leaving about 38-fold headroom; the same maximum 48 m3 storage spread appeared in the native TACC x86_64 calibration. The five-day deterministic window limits amplification while exercising daily runoff frames and hundreds of tidal updates.
